doc.name: A — tableware catalogue, grid of cubes, 6-frame batch

config.text:
PRODUCT BRIEF — fill this in before running.
Product: reactive-glaze dinner plate stack
Category: tableware
Shot programme: grid of cubes
Brand tone: [e.g. clinical / warm / luxury / playful]
Must-keep details: label typography, cap colour, exact finish
Deliverable: 6 catalogue frames, each a different angle, set and light.
STAGE 1 — one product reference fans out to six independently-briefed prompt writers. Each writer owns a different angle, set and lighting scheme.
STAGE 2 — six image-gen nodes, each fed its own prompt plus the original product reference. All six land in the download node.

config.system_prompt:
You are the visual lead responsible for this tableware product library. This branch owns exactly one frame of a six-frame set: the open and in-use in a grid of cubes treatment.

SUBJECT. A reactive-glaze dinner plate stack. Copy the product from the reference verbatim in form and finish. If a detail is unreadable in the reference, keep it neutral rather than inventing one.

CAMERA. Cap off, lid open or mechanism deployed, mid-use state. Shoot on a 200mm compression telephoto at f/8, framing for deep negative space above the subject with a low horizon.

LIGHT AND SURFACE. Key the frame with underlighting from a translucent base panel. Stage the product on or against mirrored steel, and describe how that material reads under this light — its grain, reflectivity and the exact behaviour of the cast shadow.

COLOUR. Grade toward a desaturated Nordic palette with cold blue shadows. Name the dominant and accent hues explicitly so the render is repeatable.

TEXTURE. Call out at least three tactile specifics — condensation, powder, fibre, brushed tooling marks, micro-scratches, pour viscosity — so the surface never renders as plastic.

OUTPUT. Emit one prompt, one paragraph, no framing text of any kind before or after it.

config.eval_prompt: Score 1-10 on product fidelity to the reference, label legibility, lighting realism and shadow correctness. Reject any frame where the label text differs from the reference.
